question:
A 74-year-old patient is brought in with stupor and confusion, unable to provide a medical history. Their
laboratory results show: Serum levels: - Sodium: 135 mEq/L - Potassium: 3.3 mEq/L - Chloride: 92
mEq/L - HCO3: 10 mEq/L - Serum creatinine: 4.5 mEq/L Arterial blood gas: - pH: 7.12 - PaCO2: 35
mmHg - PaO2: 77 mmHg Which acid/base disorder best describes this patient's condition? Answer
Choices: (A) Primary respiratory alkalosis with metabolic compensation (B) Primary respiratory

acidosis with metabolic compensation (C) Primary metabolic acidosis with an anion gap (D) Mixed
metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis (E) Primary metabolic acidosis without concomitant process
(F) Non-anion gap metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation (G) Primary metabolic acidosis
with concomitant respiratory acidosis (H) Mixed respiratory acidosis and metabolic alkalosis (I)
Compensated metabolic acidosis with normal respiratory function (J) Primary metabolic acidosis with
respiratory alkalosis
 A. Primary respiratory acidosis with metabolic compensation
B. Primary metabolic acidosis without concomitant process
C. Compensated metabolic acidosis with normal respiratory function
D. Primary respiratory alkalosis with metabolic compensation
E. Primary metabolic acidosis with an anion gap
F. Mixed metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis
G. Non-anion gap metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation
H. Primary metabolic acidosis with respiratory alkalosis
I. Mixed respiratory acidosis and metabolic alkalosis
J. Primary metabolic acidosis with concomitant respiratory acidosis
